R-hat of One Quantity's Draws

rhat.Rd

The rank-normalized split R-hat (Vehtari, Gelman, Simpson, Carpenter and Buerkner, 2021) of the draws of one quantity from several chains: the larger of the bulk and the folded (tail) values. It is the statistic summary.bart reports, and from four iterations on it returns the value posterior::rhat does for the inputs that function takes (see Details for the inputs where the two differ).

Usage

rhat(x)

Arguments

x

A numeric (or logical) matrix of the draws of one quantity, with a row for each iteration and a column for each chain. A vector is taken as one chain.

Details

Each chain is cut in two, the middle draw of an odd length dropped, and the draws are rank-normalized as one pool; the bulk value compares the half-chains' means and variances, and the tail value does the same on the draws folded about their median. R-hat compares each chain's spread with the pooled spread, so a value above 1 says the chains disagree.

The result is NA, as for posterior::rhat, when x has an NA, NaN or constant draws, or has a single iteration. A non-finite draw other than NA and NaN is ranked, as posterior ranks it. An argument that is not numeric or logical, is an array of more than two dimensions, or has no iteration or no chain is an error. posterior refuses a data frame and a character vector too, but takes a complex vector (and returns an infinite value with a warning for a matrix with no chain); dbarts refuses those, as they are not draws.

With two or three iterations and several chains, posterior (1.7.0) loses the dimension of its one-draw half-chains and treats each iteration as a chain; dbarts returns NA, as a half-chain of one draw has no variance. At four or more iterations the two agree to rounding.

R-hat should be read on the estimand reported: at the defaults BART's chains routinely disagree on sigma, k and single predictions, while averaged estimands, such as a subgroup's mean prediction or a contrast between subgroups, mix far better. See summary.bart.

Calling rhat

Call it as dbarts::rhat. Other packages export a function named rhat: posterior and bayesplot (and brms re-exports posterior's), and rstan exports Rhat. Whichever is attached last masks the others, and bayesplot's takes a fitted Stan model, not a matrix. The stan4bart package attaches dbarts, so it brings this name in.

Value

A single number, NA_real_ where the draws carry no information.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. and Buerkner, P.-C. (2021) Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: an improved \(\hat{R}\) for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis 16(2), 667-718.

See also

summary.bart, extract

Examples

set.seed(1)
draws <- matrix(rnorm(400), 100L, 4L)
dbarts::rhat(draws)
#> [1] 0.9948036

# four chains that disagree
dbarts::rhat(draws + rep(0:3, each = 100L))
#> [1] 1.528219
